geo-3-land-cover-land-use-and-anthropoge.title: Land cover, land use and anthropogenic biomes
geo-3-land-cover-land-use-and-anthropoge.coverage: Lesson concept checks followed by related subject revision.

questions.prompt: Land cover, land use and anthropogenic biomes — Which statement accurately explains land cover, land use and anthropogenic biomes?
options: Land cover describes the physical surface, such as forest, crops, water or buildings; land use describes its purpose. Anthropogenic biomes are ecological patterns strongly shaped by people and their activities.
Land cover and land use are interchangeable labels.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: A forest can be used for conservation or timber production; both may initially appear as forest cover. Cropland and urban settlement alter ecosystem structure and flows, but human influence also exists in apparently natural landscapes.

questions.prompt: Land cover, land use and anthropogenic biomes — Which statement is a misconception to correct?
options: Methods should be appropriate to the question and data.
Land cover and land use are interchangeable labels.
A supported conclusion should identify its evidence and scope.
questions.explanation: Land cover describes the physical surface, such as forest, crops, water or buildings; land use describes its purpose. Anthropogenic biomes are ecological patterns strongly shaped by people and their activities. A forest can be used for conservation or timber production; both may initially appear as forest cover. Cropland and urban settlement alter ecosystem structure and flows, but human influence also exists in apparently natural landscapes.

questions.prompt: Land cover and the water cycle — Which statement accurately explains land cover and the water cycle?
options: Clearing has exactly the same hydrological effect on every soil and slope.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

Vegetation intercepts rain, returns water through evapotranspiration and can support infiltration. Clearing and hard surfaces can increase rapid runoff, depending on soil, slope, rainfall and drainage.
questions.explanation: Reduced plant cover may lower interception and alter groundwater recharge; exposed soil can erode during intense rainfall. Urban drains move water quickly but can transfer downstream flood risk.

questions.prompt: Deforestation and agricultural expansion — Which statement accurately explains deforestation and agricultural expansion?
options: Deforestation converts forest to another cover; degradation reduces forest condition without necessarily removing its mapped forest class. Agricultural expansion increases area; intensification increases inputs or output on existing land.
Higher farm yields always stop forest clearing.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: New fields replace habitat and change carbon, water and soil processes. Intensification may reduce expansion pressure in some contexts but can increase fertiliser use, water demand or profitable expansion elsewhere.

questions.prompt: Urban growth and mining transformation — Which statement accurately explains urban growth and mining transformation?

Revegetation instantly restores all pre-mining ecosystem functions.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Impervious surfaces change runoff and heat exchange; excavation and waste can alter topography and water quality. Rehabilitation can improve cover yet may not restore the original ecosystem structure.

questions.prompt: Urban growth and mining transformation — Which statement is a misconception to correct?
options: Methods should be appropriate to the question and data.
Revegetation instantly restores all pre-mining ecosystem functions.
A supported conclusion should identify its evidence and scope.

Mining may remove vegetation, excavate land and create waste, roads and processing footprints. Rehabilitation can improve cover yet may not restore the original ecosystem structure.

geo-3-population-affluence-and-technolog.coverage: Lesson concept checks followed by related subject revision.

questions.prompt: Population, affluence and technology — Which statement accurately explains population, affluence and technology?
options: Population growth increases demand, while affluence changes consumption per person. Technology can improve efficiency or enable greater extraction and consumption; effects depend on institutions and behaviour.
Population growth alone fully explains every land-cover change.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: The same population can use different amounts of land through diets, housing density, waste and productivity. Efficiency gains may be partly offset by greater consumption, a rebound effect.

options: Methods should be appropriate to the question and data.
Population growth alone fully explains every land-cover change.
A supported conclusion should identify its evidence and scope.

questions.prompt: Albedo and carbon feedbacks — Which statement accurately explains albedo and carbon feedbacks?

A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

questions.prompt: Eastings, northings and grid references — Which statement accurately explains eastings, northings and grid references?
options: Grid references identify positions on a mapped grid. Read eastings first, then northings. A four-figure area reference identifies a square; a six-figure reference estimates a point to tenths within it.
Northings are read before eastings.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: For a six-figure reference, interpolate within the square rather than reading the upper-right grid line. Accuracy depends on grid scale and symbol position. Preserve leading zeroes when present.

questions.prompt: Eastings, northings and grid references — Which statement is a misconception to correct?
options: Methods should be appropriate to the question and data.
Northings are read before eastings.
A supported conclusion should identify its evidence and scope.
questions.explanation: Grid references identify positions on a mapped grid. Read eastings first, then northings. A four-figure area reference identifies a square; a six-figure reference estimates a point to tenths within it. For a six-figure reference, interpolate within the square rather than reading the upper-right grid line. Accuracy depends on grid scale and symbol position. Preserve leading zeroes when present.

questions.prompt: Eastings, northings and grid references — A point is 0.6 across from easting 24 toward 25 and 0.2 up from northing 60 toward 61. Write its four-figure and six-figure references.
options: Use the map length directly as kilometres; omit unit conversion.
Reverse the numerator and denominator and omit the stated map scale.
Read eastings first: 24, with sixth-tenth interpolation giving 246. · Read northings: 60, with second-tenth interpolation giving 602. · Area reference 2460; six-figure reference 246602.
questions.explanation: Read eastings first: 24, with sixth-tenth interpolation giving 246. · Read northings: 60, with second-tenth interpolation giving 602. · Area reference 2460; six-figure reference 246602.

questions.prompt: Biodiversity option: causes, evidence and boundaries — Which statement accurately explains biodiversity option: causes, evidence and boundaries?
options: Biodiversity change can result from natural disturbance and climate variation as well as human habitat conversion and introduced organisms. Rates and scales distinguish background change from rapid pressure.
A missing observation proves a species is globally extinct.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Fossils provide geological evidence of extinction and diversification; standardised recent surveys can reveal population or occupancy change. Shifting ecological boundaries do not guarantee species can follow them.

questions.prompt: Area from maps and unit conversion — Which statement accurately explains area from maps and unit conversion?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Area depends on the square of a length scale. One square kilometre is 1,000,000 m² or 100 hectares; one hectare is 10,000 m². Counting grid cells gives an estimate for irregular shapes.
An area scale is identical to the length scale.
questions.explanation: At 1:50,000, 1 cm is 0.5 km, so 1 cm² represents 0.25 km². Edge cells can be estimated by halves; state uncertainty rather than implying perfect precision.

questions.prompt: Climate impacts in anthropogenic environments — Which statement accurately explains climate impacts in anthropogenic environments?
options: Climate impacts are identical for all crops and households.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Agriculture and urban settlements are exposed to changing heat, water availability and extremes. Effects depend on crops, infrastructure, livelihoods and adaptive capacity.
questions.explanation: Heat can reduce labour productivity and affect crops; drought can increase irrigation demand; coastal flooding can damage assets. Adaptation may move risks between places or groups.

questions.prompt: Climate patterns: latitude, circulation and rainfall — Which statement accurately explains climate patterns: latitude, circulation and rainfall?
options: Temperature patterns reflect incoming solar energy, elevation, oceans and circulation. Rainfall patterns reflect moisture supply, uplift, atmospheric pressure and seasonal movement of circulation belts.
Latitude alone determines every place’s climate.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Warm rising air near the equator supports rain; subtropical descending air can favour dry conditions; mountains create wet windward slopes and drier rain shadows. These are broad patterns with regional exceptions.

questions.prompt: Land cover and the water cycle — Which statement accurately explains land cover and the water cycle?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

Vegetation intercepts rain, returns water through evapotranspiration and can support infiltration. Clearing and hard surfaces can increase rapid runoff, depending on soil, slope, rainfall and drainage.
Clearing has exactly the same hydrological effect on every soil and slope.
questions.explanation: Reduced plant cover may lower interception and alter groundwater recharge; exposed soil can erode during intense rainfall. Urban drains move water quickly but can transfer downstream flood risk.

questions.prompt: Climate evidence over geological and recent time — Which statement accurately explains climate evidence over geological and recent time?
options: A temperature anomaly is the same as a place’s absolute temperature.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Proxy records infer past climate indirectly; instruments measure selected variables directly. Geological-scale and recent evidence differ in resolution, geographic coverage and uncertainty.
questions.explanation: Ice-core gases reveal past atmospheric composition; isotopic records provide temperature-related information. Recent instrumental records combine station and ocean measurements using adjustments and stated baselines.

questions.prompt: Map conventions, atlas choices and sketch maps — Which statement accurately explains map conventions, atlas choices and sketch maps?
options: A usable map states title, orientation, legend, scale and source, usually within a border. An atlas can supply location and thematic context, but its scale and date determine usefulness.
Every image that looks like a map can be used for accurate measurement.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: A sketch map simplifies features to support an argument; symbols and annotations should explain relationships rather than reproduce decoration. A schematic is not suitable for precise distance calculations unless a scale is supplied.

questions.prompt: Compass directions and bearings — Which statement accurately explains compass directions and bearings?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Compass direction expresses orientation; a bearing is an angle measured clockwise from north, normally written with three digits. Sixteen-point directions divide the compass into 22.5° sectors.
Bearings are measured anticlockwise from east.
questions.explanation: East is 090°, south 180° and west 270°. A reverse bearing differs by 180° with adjustment to the 000–359° range. Distinguish grid, true and magnetic north when a map supplies them.

questions.prompt: Contours, landforms and slope shape — Which statement accurately explains contours, landforms and slope shape?
options: Every closed contour must be a hill, regardless of map symbols.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Contours join points of equal elevation. Close spacing indicates a steeper slope for the same contour interval; valleys and spurs have different contour shapes. Spot heights give point elevations.
questions.explanation: A valley’s contour V usually points uphill; a spur’s projection points downhill. Concave slopes steepen uphill and flatten toward the foot; convex slopes are gentler near the top and steeper lower down.

questions.prompt: Biodiversity option: impacts and responses — Which statement accurately explains biodiversity option: impacts and responses?
options: Biodiversity loss can reduce ecosystem resilience, pollination, food resources and culturally valued relationships. Effects in natural ecosystems and managed agriculture can interact.
One protected patch is enough to conserve every species and ecosystem service.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Corridors and protected habitats can reduce fragmentation; biosecurity can reduce invasion risk. Agricultural diversification, altered practices and restored habitat can support adaptation, with local trade-offs.

questions.prompt: Two climate mitigation pathways — Which statement accurately explains two climate mitigation pathways?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Climate mitigation reduces greenhouse-gas emissions or increases durable removals. Energy decarbonisation and protection of carbon-rich ecosystems target different sources and sinks.
A planted tree immediately cancels any quantity of fossil emissions.
questions.explanation: Low-emission electricity can displace fossil generation; reduced clearing avoids emissions and preserves stores. Additionality, leakage and permanence matter when evaluating claimed carbon benefits.

questions.prompt: Policies, ownership and contrasting countries — Which statement accurately explains policies, ownership and contrasting countries?
options: Countries with similar climates must experience identical clearing rates.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

Government policy and land ownership influence who can clear land, who gains benefits and who bears costs. Culture, ideology and economic structure can also shape decisions, but explanations need evidence.
questions.explanation: Enforcement of conservation rules may limit conversion; insecure tenure can discourage long-term investment or encourage contested claims. Public, private and customary ownership are not inherently sustainable or unsustainable.

questions.prompt: Gradient ratios and cross sections — Which statement accurately explains gradient ratios and cross sections?
options: Average gradient compares vertical change with horizontal distance in the same units. Express 1:n by dividing horizontal distance by vertical change. A cross section plots elevations along a line through terrain.
A gradient of 1:100 is steeper than 1:20.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: The smaller the n in 1:n, the steeper the slope. Cross sections show relief and annotated cultural features; vertical exaggeration can make slopes appear steeper than reality.

questions.prompt: Three adaptation pathways — Which statement accurately explains three adaptation pathways?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Adaptation reduces harm from actual or expected climate impacts. Water-demand management, heat-sensitive urban design and agricultural adjustment target different exposure or sensitivity pathways.
Adaptation reduces greenhouse-gas emissions by definition.
questions.explanation: Efficient irrigation can reduce water used per unit output; shade and ventilation can reduce heat exposure; changed planting or crop choice can respond to seasons. Each can have limits, rebound effects or unequal access.

questions.prompt: Latitude, longitude and degrees–minutes — Which statement accurately explains latitude, longitude and degrees–minutes?
options: Minutes can be converted by dividing by 100.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Latitude measures angular distance north or south of the equator; longitude measures angular distance east or west of the prime meridian. One degree contains 60 minutes, not 100.
questions.explanation: A coordinate needs hemisphere or signed convention. Angular differences are not automatically equal ground distances: longitude distance changes with latitude. Latitude-longitude is different from a local grid reference.

questions.prompt: Atmospheric circulation and the hydrological cycle — Which statement accurately explains atmospheric circulation and the hydrological cycle?
options: Differential heating drives large-scale atmospheric circulation, redistributing heat and moisture. The water cycle links evaporation, condensation, precipitation, storage and runoff.
All rain falling in a region comes directly from the nearest ocean.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Rising air cools and can condense moisture; descending air warms and can inhibit clouds. Seasonal shifts, oceans and terrain complicate idealised circulation cells. Land-cover change can modify moisture transfer.

questions.prompt: Albedo and carbon feedbacks — Which statement accurately explains albedo and carbon feedbacks?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Albedo is the fraction of incoming shortwave radiation reflected. Land-cover changes can alter albedo, carbon stores, evapotranspiration and roughness simultaneously, with competing effects.
Higher albedo means all effects of clearing are environmentally beneficial.
questions.explanation: Ice loss exposes darker surfaces and increases absorption, a positive feedback. Clearing can increase reflectivity but release carbon and reduce moisture transfer; the net effect depends on place and timescale.

questions.prompt: Biodiversity option: causes, evidence and boundaries — Which statement accurately explains biodiversity option: causes, evidence and boundaries?
options: Biodiversity change can result from natural disturbance and climate variation as well as human habitat conversion and introduced organisms. Rates and scales distinguish background change from rapid pressure.
A missing observation proves a species is globally extinct.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Fossils provide geological evidence of extinction and diversification; standardised recent surveys can reveal population or occupancy change. Shifting ecological boundaries do not guarantee species can follow them.

questions.prompt: Area from maps and unit conversion — Which statement accurately explains area from maps and unit conversion?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

An area scale is identical to the length scale.
questions.explanation: At 1:50,000, 1 cm is 0.5 km, so 1 cm² represents 0.25 km². Edge cells can be estimated by halves; state uncertainty rather than implying perfect precision.

questions.prompt: Climate impacts in anthropogenic environments — Which statement accurately explains climate impacts in anthropogenic environments?
options: Climate impacts are identical for all crops and households.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Agriculture and urban settlements are exposed to changing heat, water availability and extremes. Effects depend on crops, infrastructure, livelihoods and adaptive capacity.
questions.explanation: Heat can reduce labour productivity and affect crops; drought can increase irrigation demand; coastal flooding can damage assets. Adaptation may move risks between places or groups.

questions.prompt: Climate patterns: latitude, circulation and rainfall — Which statement accurately explains climate patterns: latitude, circulation and rainfall?
options: Temperature patterns reflect incoming solar energy, elevation, oceans and circulation. Rainfall patterns reflect moisture supply, uplift, atmospheric pressure and seasonal movement of circulation belts.
Latitude alone determines every place’s climate.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Warm rising air near the equator supports rain; subtropical descending air can favour dry conditions; mountains create wet windward slopes and drier rain shadows. These are broad patterns with regional exceptions.

questions.prompt: Land cover and the water cycle — Which statement accurately explains land cover and the water cycle?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

Vegetation intercepts rain, returns water through evapotranspiration and can support infiltration. Clearing and hard surfaces can increase rapid runoff, depending on soil, slope, rainfall and drainage.
Clearing has exactly the same hydrological effect on every soil and slope.
questions.explanation: Reduced plant cover may lower interception and alter groundwater recharge; exposed soil can erode during intense rainfall. Urban drains move water quickly but can transfer downstream flood risk.

questions.prompt: Climate evidence over geological and recent time — Which statement accurately explains climate evidence over geological and recent time?
options: A temperature anomaly is the same as a place’s absolute temperature.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Proxy records infer past climate indirectly; instruments measure selected variables directly. Geological-scale and recent evidence differ in resolution, geographic coverage and uncertainty.
questions.explanation: Ice-core gases reveal past atmospheric composition; isotopic records provide temperature-related information. Recent instrumental records combine station and ocean measurements using adjustments and stated baselines.

questions.prompt: Map conventions, atlas choices and sketch maps — Which statement accurately explains map conventions, atlas choices and sketch maps?

A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

questions.prompt: Contours, landforms and slope shape — Which statement accurately explains contours, landforms and slope shape?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

Every closed contour must be a hill, regardless of map symbols.
questions.explanation: A valley’s contour V usually points uphill; a spur’s projection points downhill. Concave slopes steepen uphill and flatten toward the foot; convex slopes are gentler near the top and steeper lower down.

questions.prompt: Biodiversity option: impacts and responses — Which statement accurately explains biodiversity option: impacts and responses?

A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

questions.explanation: Corridors and protected habitats can reduce fragmentation; biosecurity can reduce invasion risk. Agricultural diversification, altered practices and restored habitat can support adaptation, with local trade-offs.

questions.prompt: Eastings, northings and grid references — Which statement accurately explains eastings, northings and grid references?

A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

questions.prompt: Two climate mitigation pathways — Which statement accurately explains two climate mitigation pathways?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Climate mitigation reduces greenhouse-gas emissions or increases durable removals. Energy decarbonisation and protection of carbon-rich ecosystems target different sources and sinks.
A planted tree immediately cancels any quantity of fossil emissions.
questions.explanation: Low-emission electricity can displace fossil generation; reduced clearing avoids emissions and preserves stores. Additionality, leakage and permanence matter when evaluating claimed carbon benefits.

questions.prompt: Policies, ownership and contrasting countries — Which statement accurately explains policies, ownership and contrasting countries?
options: Countries with similar climates must experience identical clearing rates.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

questions.prompt: Gradient ratios and cross sections — Which statement accurately explains gradient ratios and cross sections?

A gradient of 1:100 is steeper than 1:20.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

questions.prompt: Three adaptation pathways — Which statement accurately explains three adaptation pathways?

Adaptation reduces greenhouse-gas emissions by definition.
questions.explanation: Efficient irrigation can reduce water used per unit output; shade and ventilation can reduce heat exposure; changed planting or crop choice can respond to seasons. Each can have limits, rebound effects or unequal access.

questions.prompt: Latitude, longitude and degrees–minutes — Which statement accurately explains latitude, longitude and degrees–minutes?

A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

questions.prompt: Atmospheric circulation and the hydrological cycle — Which statement accurately explains atmospheric circulation and the hydrological cycle?

All rain falling in a region comes directly from the nearest ocean.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

questions.prompt: Albedo and carbon feedbacks — Which statement accurately explains albedo and carbon feedbacks?

geo-4-change-statistics-descriptive-stat.title: Change statistics, descriptive statistics and frequency
geo-4-change-statistics-descriptive-stat.coverage: Lesson concept checks followed by related subject revision.

questions.prompt: Change statistics, descriptive statistics and frequency — Which statement accurately explains change statistics, descriptive statistics and frequency?
options: Mean is sum divided by count; median is the middle ordered value; mode is the most frequent; range is maximum minus minimum. Percent change uses the initial value as the denominator.
A rise from 40% to 60% is always described accurately as a 20% increase.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Outliers can pull the mean away from typical observations; frequencies describe how often values or classes occur. A change in percentage points differs from relative percentage change.

questions.prompt: Change statistics, descriptive statistics and frequency — Which statement is a misconception to correct?
options: Methods should be appropriate to the question and data.
A rise from 40% to 60% is always described accurately as a 20% increase.
A supported conclusion should identify its evidence and scope.
questions.explanation: Mean is sum divided by count; median is the middle ordered value; mode is the most frequent; range is maximum minus minimum. Percent change uses the initial value as the denominator. Outliers can pull the mean away from typical observations; frequencies describe how often values or classes occur. A change in percentage points differs from relative percentage change.

questions.prompt: Change statistics, descriptive statistics and frequency — Journey minutes are 8, 10, 10, 12, 25. Find mean, median, mode and range; explain which statistic is pulled upward by the longest journey.
options: Use the map length directly as kilometres; omit unit conversion.
Reverse the numerator and denominator and omit the stated map scale.
Sum = 65; mean = 65/5 = 13 minutes. · Median = 10; mode = 10. · Range = 25 − 8 = 17 minutes. · The mean is pulled upward by the 25-minute journey; the median is more resistant to this extreme.
questions.explanation: Sum = 65; mean = 65/5 = 13 minutes. · Median = 10; mode = 10. · Range = 25 − 8 = 17 minutes. · The mean is pulled upward by the 25-minute journey; the median is more resistant to this extreme.

questions.prompt: Photographs, radar, satellite images and change — Which statement accurately explains photographs, radar, satellite images and change?
options: Ground photographs show local detail but limited area; vertical aerial images support plan view; oblique images show perspective with variable scale. Satellite and radar products observe wider patterns with sensor-specific properties.
Every brown pixel in a satellite image indicates deforestation.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Image colour is not necessarily natural colour; radar responds to surface properties and geometry. Topographic maps add symbols, heights and names. Pairing images and maps can strengthen interpretation.

questions.prompt: Australia’s settlement distribution — Which statement accurately explains australia’s settlement distribution?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

Australia’s settlement pattern reflects coastal access, water, climate, history, economic opportunities and transport. Historical and cultural processes include First Nations relationships and colonial settlement patterns.
Climate alone explains Australia’s settlement pattern.
questions.explanation: Ports and railways supported coastal cities; inland resource and agricultural centres grew around particular opportunities. Water and extreme conditions constrain some settlement but do not alone explain every town.

questions.prompt: Regional challenge: population loss and service provision — Which statement accurately explains regional challenge: population loss and service provision?
options: Population decline only reduces traffic and has no social costs.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Population loss can shrink a service catchment, reduce local spending and change workforce availability. A declining population may also age as younger people leave.
questions.explanation: Service closure can encourage further departure, creating a feedback loop. Distance and transport barriers can magnify the effect, although remote delivery or regional cooperation may help.

questions.prompt: Graphs, correlation and causal claims — Which statement accurately explains graphs, correlation and causal claims?
options: Graph choice depends on data: lines for ordered time, bars for categories, histograms for grouped continuous values, scatterplots for association, and population pyramids for age-sex structure.
A strong correlation establishes a causal mechanism without other evidence.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Correlation describes co-variation, not proof of cause. Shared drivers, reverse causation and sampling can produce associations. Climate graphs combine rainfall columns and temperature lines with separate axes.

questions.prompt: Mumbai: demographic variation and informal livelihoods — Which statement accurately explains mumbai: demographic variation and informal livelihoods?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

A megacity can contain substantial differences in income, age, culture and access to services. Informal employment and housing reflect complex constraints and opportunities; residents should not be represented as one uniform group.
Everyone in informal housing has the same livelihood and needs.
questions.explanation: Migration, housing costs, employment access and planning shape distributions. Official counts can omit some informal activities, so quantitative evidence should be combined with careful local accounts.

questions.prompt: Perth transport: stakeholders and liveability evaluation — Which statement accurately explains perth transport: stakeholders and liveability evaluation?
options: The most vocal stakeholder necessarily represents every resident.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

Stakeholders can value different outcomes, such as access, quiet streets, business activity, cost and environmental protection. Evaluation weighs evidence, distribution and time rather than counting supportive opinions.
questions.explanation: Residents may support access yet oppose tree loss; commuters may value faster trips; non-drivers may prioritise frequency and affordability. Planning should identify whose benefits and burdens are missing.

questions.prompt: Regional challenge: housing and social vulnerability — Which statement accurately explains regional challenge: housing and social vulnerability?
options: Housing challenges can combine limited supply, unsuitable dwellings, high costs and uneven access. Remoteness and employment cycles can influence prices, maintenance and service provision.
A town with empty houses cannot have a housing problem.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: A resource boom can attract workers faster than housing is built; vulnerable residents may face displacement. A downturn can leave vacant properties that remain unaffordable or unsuitable for those needing them.

questions.prompt: Perth: demographic evidence and planning needs — Which statement accurately explains perth: demographic evidence and planning needs?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Perth’s demographic analysis should use a defined metropolitan boundary and dated census data. Age, gender, socioeconomic and cultural distributions help explain differentiated planning needs.
A census-area average accurately describes every household within it.
questions.explanation: Services need to account for both proportions and absolute populations. Area averages can conceal vulnerable households; boundary changes can distort apparent growth between censuses.

questions.prompt: Perth water strategy two: replenishment and demand management — Which statement accurately explains perth water strategy two: replenishment and demand management?
options: Water efficiency guarantees total demand falls even if population and use grow.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

Groundwater replenishment treats wastewater to a high standard and recharges aquifers under regulated monitoring. Demand management reduces unnecessary use through infrastructure, practices and pricing design.
questions.explanation: Recycling adds a source and can reduce some pressures, while efficiency lowers demand per activity. Public trust, treatment assurance, energy and aquifer conditions require attention; saving per device need not equal lower total demand.

questions.prompt: Urbanisation and urban growth — Which statement accurately explains urbanisation and urban growth?
options: Urbanisation is an increase in the proportion of people living in urban places; urban population growth is an increase in their number. Migration, natural increase and reclassification can change both, but not identically.
Any increase in city population necessarily means greater urbanisation.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: An urban population can grow while its national proportion falls if rural population grows faster. Definitions of urban areas vary, so comparisons need consistent boundaries and criteria.

questions.prompt: Statistical maps: choropleth, dots and circles — Which statement accurately explains statistical maps: choropleth, dots and circles?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

A choropleth shades defined areas by a statistic; dot maps represent quantities or distributions; proportional circles vary symbol area to show magnitude. Isolines join equal values on a continuous surface.
A larger absolute case count always means a higher per-person risk.
questions.explanation: Rates are often suitable for choropleths when areas have different populations; absolute counts can be misleading. Circle area, not radius, should be proportional to the value, so radius is proportional to the square root.

questions.prompt: Regional challenge: economic restructuring and employment — Which statement accurately explains regional challenge: economic restructuring and employment?
options: Higher production always means more local jobs.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

Economic restructuring changes the composition of activity, such as movement from labour-intensive farming or manufacturing to other sectors. Employment effects depend on skills, ownership and new opportunities.
questions.explanation: Automation can increase output while reducing some jobs; mine closure can reduce demand for contractors and retail. Retraining helps only if accessible jobs and support exist.

questions.prompt: Mumbai challenge two: water and unequal service access — Which statement accurately explains mumbai challenge two: water and unequal service access?
options: Urban water challenges can include supply reliability, distribution losses, affordability, sanitation links and unequal household access. A city-wide average can conceal neighbourhood differences.
If the city has enough total water, every household must have reliable access.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Intermittent service can increase storage needs; leakage wastes treated supply; insecure housing can complicate connections. Rainfall and catchment conditions interact with governance and infrastructure.

questions.prompt: Perth transport strategy one: connected centres and infill — Which statement accurately explains perth transport strategy one: connected centres and infill?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.

Infill and connected centres aim to use existing infrastructure and place more homes near services and employment. WA’s Perth and Peel planning framework links growth with land use and infrastructure.
All infill development is automatically sustainable and affordable.
questions.explanation: Shorter or better-connected trips can support public and active transport. Benefits depend on affordable housing, street design, service capacity and retaining amenities, not simply adding dwellings.

questions.prompt: Mumbai strategy evaluation and comparison with Perth — Which statement accurately explains mumbai strategy evaluation and comparison with perth?
options: A successful strategy can be copied unchanged into every city.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Comparing cities requires the same challenge and criteria but different local conditions. Strategy transfer should be conditional on climate, urban form, finance, rights and institutions.
questions.explanation: Perth and Mumbai water and transport pressures have different infrastructure histories and distributions. Similar aims such as reliable access can require different combinations of technology and governance.

questions.prompt: Urban sprawl, inertia and land-use competition — Which statement accurately explains urban sprawl, inertia and land-use competition?
options: Urban sprawl extends development outward, often at low density. Inertia describes persistence of established land uses despite changing pressures; competition occurs when uses seek the same scarce land.
Any unused-looking site is available for housing without cost.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Existing buildings, ownership, infrastructure and regulations can slow change. Housing, industry, conservation and recreation compete over accessible sites, with different benefits and external costs.

questions.prompt: Perth water strategy one: desalination — Which statement accurately explains perth water strategy one: desalination?
options: A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
Desalination supplies water from seawater and reduces dependence on rainfall runoff. Sustainability evaluation includes energy, emissions, marine impacts, costs and resilience.
Rainfall-independent means impact-free and infrastructure-independent.
questions.explanation: A rainfall-independent source still depends on power, infrastructure and maintenance. Renewable energy arrangements can reduce emissions but do not remove every ecological or financial impact.

questions.prompt: Population pyramids, climate graphs and synoptic charts — Which statement accurately explains population pyramids, climate graphs and synoptic charts?
options: A population pyramid shows age structure split by sex or gender categories defined by its source; a climate graph shows monthly temperature and rainfall; a synoptic chart shows pressure and weather systems at a time.
A single synoptic chart represents the long-term climate.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Compare units and denominators in pyramids; annual rainfall is the sum of monthly rainfall and temperature range is maximum minus minimum monthly mean. Close isobars suggest a stronger pressure gradient, not an exact wind speed.

questions.prompt: GIS overlays, source quality and ethical fieldwork — Which statement accurately explains gis overlays, source quality and ethical fieldwork?
options: GIS overlays combine locations and attributes, but coordinate systems, dates, resolution and definitions must align. Fieldwork provides local evidence and should use consistent methods with consent and privacy.
Combining many layers makes poor-quality data automatically valid.
A place’s name alone establishes its processes and outcomes.
questions.explanation: Reliability concerns consistency; validity concerns whether evidence answers the inquiry. Triangulation combines independent sources, while reference logs identify author, date, method and limitations.

questions.prompt: GIS overlays, source quality and ethical fieldwork — Which statement is a misconception to correct?
options: Methods should be appropriate to the question and data.
Combining many layers makes poor-quality data automatically valid.
A supported conclusion should identify its evidence and scope.
questions.explanation: GIS overlays combine locations and attributes, but coordinate systems, dates, resolution and definitions must align.
